question.problem:
Let $D$ be the finite region bounded by the curve 
$({x}^{3}+y)^{2}+y=3$ and the line $y=2.$ Consider the transformation $T,$ given by

$$
T:(u,v)\to (x(u,v),y(u,v)),
$$

where $u={x}^{3}+y$ and $v=2-y.$ Find the representation of ${T}^{-1}(D)$ in the $uv$-plane.
question.worked_solution:
First, notice that we are given that 

$$
{T}^{-1}:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{x}^{3}+y \\ 2-y\end{aligned}].
$$

Substituting ${x}^{3}+y=u$ and $y=2-v$ into the equation of the first curve, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}({x}^{3}+y)^{2}+y=3\,⟹\,{u}^{2}+2-v=3\,⟹\,v={u}^{2}-1,\end{aligned}
$$

while substituting $y=2-v$ into the equation of the second curve, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}y=2\,⟹\,2-v=2\,⟹\,v=0.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the intersections of the curves in the $uv$-plane, we solve the following system:

$$
\begin{aligned}\{\begin{aligned}v={u}^{2}-1 \\ v=0\end{aligned}\,⟹\,\{\begin{aligned}u=\pm 1 \\ v=0.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the intersection points are $(\pm 1,0).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14166956/assets/60d8d3e30eba31683d1b6bb9bf399aa20f2bda37be1cb31bec431a4e27c0f54e.png)

As a result, our domain in the $uv$-plane has the type I representation 

$$
{T}^{-1}(D)=\{(u,v)\,:\,-1\le u\le 1,\,{u}^{2}-1\le v\le 0\}.
$$
